verses.1:1: To the brothers, the Jews throughout Egypt: the brothers, the Jews in Jerusalem and those in the country of Judea, wish greetings and good peace.
verses.1:2: And may God do good to you, and remember His covenant with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, His faithful servants.
verses.1:3: And may He give you all a heart to worship Him and to do His will with a great heart and a willing soul;
verses.1:4: and may He open your heart in His law and in the statutes, and may He make peace;
verses.1:5: and may He hear your petitions, and be reconciled to you, and not forsake you in an evil time.
verses.1:6: And now we are here praying for you.
verses.1:7: When Demetrius was reigning, in the one hundred sixty-ninth year, we, the Jews, wrote to you in the distress and in the crisis that came upon us in these years, since Jason and those with him revolted from the holy land and the kingdom,
verses.1:8: and burned the gateway and shed innocent blood. And we petitioned the Lord and were heard; we offered sacrifice and fine flour, and brought out the lamps, and set out the loaves.
verses.1:9: And now, see that you observe the days of the festival of Booths of the month of Chislev.
verses.1:10: In the eighty-eighth year, in Jerusalem. And those in Judea and the council of elders and Judas, to Aristobulus, teacher of King Ptolemy, who is from the lineage of the anointed priests, and to the Jews in Egypt, greetings and good health.
verses.1:11: Having been saved by God from great dangers, we greatly give thanks to Him, as those arrayed in battle against a king.
verses.1:12: For He Himself drove out into Persia those who were arrayed in battle in the holy city.
verses.1:13: For when the leader arrived, and the force around him that seemed to be irresistible, they were cut to pieces in the temple of Nanea, since the priests attending Nanea used deception.
verses.1:14: For as though to marry her, Antiochus and the friends with him came to the place for the sake of taking the large sums of money by way of a dowry.
verses.1:15: And when the priests of the shrine of Nanea had set them out, and he had approached with a few men into the enclosure of the sacred precinct, they shut up the temple when Antiochus entered,
verses.1:16: opened the hidden door of the paneled ceiling, and throwing stones, struck down the leader as with a thunderbolt, dismembering them and throwing the heads to those outside.
verses.1:17: In every way blessed be our God, who gave over those who acted impiously.
verses.1:18: As we are about to observe on the twenty-fifth of Chislev the purification of the temple, we thought it necessary to inform you, so that you yourselves also may observe the festival of Booths and of the fire, when Nehemiah, who at that time built the temple and the altar, offered sacrifices.
verses.1:19: For indeed, when our fathers were being led away into Persia, the devout priests secretly took some of the fire of the altar and hid it in a hollow having the form of a waterless cistern, in which they secured it so that the place was unknown to all.
verses.1:20: And after many years had passed, when it seemed good to God, Nehemiah, having been sent by the king of Persia, sent the descendants of the priests who had hidden it for the fire.
verses.1:21: When they informed us that they had not found fire, but thick water, he commanded them to draw some out and bring it. And when the materials of the sacrifices had been brought up, Nehemiah commanded the priests to sprinkle with the water both the wood and the things laid upon it.
verses.1:22: And when it was done and time had passed, and the sun shone out though it was clouded over, a great fire was kindled, so that all marveled.
verses.1:23: And the priests offered a prayer while the sacrifice was being consumed, both the priests and everyone, with Jonathan leading and the rest responding, just as Nehemiah did.
verses.1:24: And the prayer was in this manner: "Lord God, Creator of all things, awesome and mighty and righteous and merciful, the only King and gracious One,
verses.1:25: the only Provider, the only righteous and almighty and eternal One, who delivers Israel from every evil, who made the fathers chosen ones and sanctified them:
verses.1:26: Accept the sacrifice on behalf of all Your people Israel, and guard Your portion and consecrate it.
verses.1:27: Gather together our dispersion, free those who are enslaved among the nations, look upon the despised and detested, and let the nations know that You are our God.
verses.1:28: Torment those who oppress and behave insolently in arrogance;
verses.1:29: plant Your people in Your holy place, just as Moses said."
verses.1:30: And the priests were singing the hymns.
verses.1:31: And when the materials of the sacrifice had been consumed, Nehemiah commanded that the remaining water also be poured over large stones.
verses.1:32: And when this was done, a flame was kindled; but when the light from the altar shone back, it was consumed.
verses.1:33: And when the matter became known, and it was reported to the king of the Persians that in the place where the priests who had been carried away hid the fire, the water had appeared, with which Nehemiah and those with him also purified the sacrifices,
verses.1:34: the king enclosed it and made it sacred, after verifying the matter.
verses.1:35: And to those from whom the king received many valuables, he also gave a share.
verses.1:36: And Nehemiah and those with him named this Nephthar, which is translated Purification; and by most people it is called Nephthar.
verses.2:1: Now it is found in the records that Jeremiah the prophet commanded those who were deported to take some of the fire, as has been indicated,
verses.2:2: and how the prophet charged those who were deported, after giving them the law, that they should not forget the statutes of the Lord, and that they should not be led astray in their minds when seeing images of gold and silver and the adornment around them.
verses.2:3: And saying other similar things, he urged them not to let the law depart from their heart.
verses.2:4: And it was in the writing that the prophet, after a divine oracle had come to him, commanded the tabernacle and the ark to follow along, and how he went out to the mountain where Moses went up and viewed the inheritance of God.
verses.2:5: And when Jeremiah came, he found a cave-like dwelling, and he brought the tabernacle and the ark and the altar of incense in there, and blocked up the entrance.
verses.2:6: And some of those who were following along came up in order to mark the way, and they were not able to find it.
verses.2:7: And when Jeremiah learned of it, he rebuked them and said, "Indeed, the place will be unknown until God gathers the assembly of the people and mercy comes.
verses.2:8: And then the Lord will reveal these things, and the glory of the Lord and the cloud will appear, as it was shown in the time of Moses, and as Solomon also asked, that the place might be greatly consecrated."
verses.2:9: And it was also made clear how, having wisdom, he offered a sacrifice of dedication and of the completion of the temple.
verses.2:10: Just as Moses also prayed to the Lord, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the materials of the sacrifice, so Solomon prayed to the Lord, and the fire came down and consumed the burnt offerings.
verses.2:11: And Moses said, "Because the sin offering had not been eaten, it was consumed."
verses.2:12: Likewise Solomon also observed the eight days.
verses.2:13: And the same things were also recounted in the archives and in the memoirs concerning Nehemiah, and how, founding a library, he gathered together the books about the kings and prophets, and those of David, and letters of kings concerning dedicated offerings.
verses.2:14: And likewise Judas also gathered together these things that had been scattered because of the war that happened to us, and they are with us.
verses.2:15: Therefore, if you have need of any of these, send those who will bring them to you.
verses.2:16: As we are about to observe the purification, therefore, we have written to you; you will therefore do well to observe the days.
verses.2:17: Now God is the One who saved all His people and restored His inheritance to all, and the kingdom and the priesthood and the sanctification,
verses.2:18: just as He promised through the law. For we hope in God that He will soon have mercy on us and gather us together from under heaven into the holy place, for He has rescued us from great evils and purified the place.
verses.2:19: Now the events concerning Judas Maccabeus and his brothers, and the purification of the greatest temple, and the dedication of the altar,
verses.2:20: and furthermore the wars against Antiochus Epiphanes and his son Eupator,
verses.2:21: and the manifestations that occurred from heaven to those who acted bravely with zeal for Judaism, so that, though few, they plundered the whole country and pursued the barbarian multitudes,
verses.2:22: and recovered the temple renowned throughout the whole inhabited world, and freed the city, and re-established the laws that were about to be abolished, as the Lord became gracious to them with all clemency,
verses.2:23: having been set forth by Jason of Cyrene in five books, we will try to abridge in a single volume.
verses.2:24: For considering the flood of numbers, and the difficulty that exists for those who wish to plunge into the narratives of the history because of the abundance of the material,
verses.2:25: we have aimed at enjoyment for those who wish to read, ease for those who take pleasure in committing it to memory, and benefit for all who encounter it.
verses.2:26: And for us who have undertaken the hard labor of the abridgment, it is not easy, but the matter is one of sweat and sleeplessness,
verses.2:27: just as for the one who prepares a banquet and seeks the advantage of others it is not effortless; nevertheless, for the sake of the gratitude of the many, we will gladly endure the hard labor,
verses.2:28: leaving the exact inquiry concerning each detail to the author, while growing weary in following the outlines of the abridgment.
verses.2:29: For just as the architect of a new house must take care for the whole structure, while the one who undertakes to dedicate and paint it must examine what is suitable for ornamentation, so I think it is with us also.
verses.2:30: To enter in, and to walk about in discourse, and to inquire closely into the particulars belongs to the originator of the history;
verses.2:31: but to pursue brevity of expression and to decline exhaustive treatment of the subject matter must be granted to the one making the paraphrase.
verses.2:32: From this point, therefore, let us begin the narrative, having added this much to what has been said before; for it is foolish to be lengthy before the history, while abridging the history.
verses.3:1: While the holy city was inhabited in complete peace, and the laws were kept most excellently because of the piety and hatred of wickedness of Onias the high priest,
verses.3:2: it came about that even the kings themselves honored the place and glorified the temple with the finest gifts,
verses.3:3: so that even Seleucus, the king of Asia, supplied from his own revenues all the expenses falling due for the services of the sacrifices.
verses.3:4: But a certain Simon from the tribe of Benjamin, who had been appointed overseer of the temple, had a dispute with the high priest concerning the administration of the market in the city.
verses.3:5: And being unable to overcome Onias, he went to Apollonius son of Thraseas, who at that time was governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.
verses.3:6: And he reported that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of untold money, so that the amount of the funds was beyond counting, and that they did not contribute to the account of the sacrifices, and that it was possible for these to fall under the authority of the king.
verses.3:7: When Apollonius met with the king, he informed him about the money that had been disclosed to him; and the king, having chosen Heliodorus, who was in charge of state affairs, sent him, giving orders to carry out the removal of the aforementioned money.
verses.3:8: Immediately Heliodorus set out on the journey, in appearance as though to inspect the cities throughout Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, but in reality to carry out the purpose of the king.
verses.3:9: When he arrived in Jerusalem and was warmly received by the high priest of the city, he told him about the information that had been given and made clear for what reason he was present; and he inquired whether in truth these things actually were so.
verses.3:10: When the high priest explained that these were deposits of widows and orphans,
verses.3:11: and that some also belonged to Hyrcanus son of Tobias, a man of very high standing (not as the impious Simon was falsely reporting), and that in all there were four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold,
verses.3:12: and that it was altogether impossible to wrong those who had trusted in the holiness of the place and in the majesty and inviolability of the temple honored throughout the entire world,
verses.3:13: the other man, because of the royal orders he had, kept saying that these must by all means be taken into the royal treasury.
verses.3:14: Having appointed a day, he went in to direct the inspection concerning these things; and there was no small anguish throughout the whole city.
verses.3:15: And the priests, throwing themselves down before the altar in their priestly robes, called out toward heaven to the One who gave the law concerning deposits to keep these safe for those who had deposited them.
verses.3:16: And to see the appearance of the high priest was to be wounded in mind; for his face and his altered color revealed the anguish in his soul.
verses.3:17: For a certain dread and shuddering of body had enveloped the man, through which the pain present in his heart became clearly evident to those looking on.
verses.3:18: And people were rushing out of their houses in crowds for public supplication, so that the place would not be about to come into contempt.
verses.3:19: And the women, with sackcloth wrapped beneath their breasts, thronged along the streets; and of the virgins who were kept indoors, some ran together to the gates, others to the walls, and some peered out through the windows.
verses.3:20: And all of them, stretching out their hands toward heaven, were making their petition.
verses.3:21: And one had to pity the mingled prostration of the multitude and the suspense of the greatly anguished high priest.
verses.3:22: So they were calling upon the almighty Lord to keep the things entrusted safe for those who had entrusted them, with complete security.
verses.3:23: But Heliodorus was carrying out what had been decided.
verses.3:24: Now when he was already present right there with his bodyguards by the treasury, the Sovereign of spirits and of all authority made a great manifestation, so that all who had dared to come along, struck with terror at the power of God, were turned to faintness and cowardice.
verses.3:25: For a horse appeared to them, having a terrifying rider and adorned with the finest trappings; and rushing fiercely, it struck at Heliodorus with its front hooves, while the one seated upon it appeared to have full armor of gold.
verses.3:26: And two other young men appeared to him, remarkable in strength, finest in speech, and splendid in apparel; and standing on either side, they flogged him unceasingly, inflicting many blows upon him.
verses.3:27: And when he suddenly fell to the ground and was enveloped in deep darkness, they snatched him up and placed him in a litter,
verses.3:28: and they carried away the man who had just entered the aforementioned treasury with a great retinue and all his bodyguard, him who had now become completely helpless and had clearly recognized the sovereign power.
verses.3:29: And because of the divine working he lay cast down, speechless and deprived of all hope and deliverance;
verses.3:30: while they were blessing the Lord, who marvelously glorifies His own place. And the temple, which a little before was full of dread and turmoil, now that the Lord Almighty had appeared, was filled with joy and gladness.
verses.3:31: Quickly some of Heliodorus's companions begged Onias to call upon the Most High and to grant life to the one lying altogether at his last breath.
verses.3:32: And the high priest, becoming apprehensive that the king might form a suspicion that some foul play had been perpetrated against Heliodorus by the Jews, offered a sacrifice for the man's deliverance.
verses.3:33: While the high priest was making the atonement, the same young men appeared again to Heliodorus, dressed in the same garments, and standing there, they said, "Give great thanks to Onias the high priest, for because of him the Lord has granted you life.
verses.3:34: And you, having been flogged from heaven, declare to all the majestic might of God." And having said these things, they vanished from sight.
verses.3:35: Then Heliodorus, having offered a sacrifice to God, and having vowed the greatest vows to the One who had preserved his life, and having warmly acknowledged Onias, marched back with his forces to the king;
verses.3:36: and he testified openly to all about the deeds of the supreme God that he had seen before his eyes.
verses.3:37: When the king asked Heliodorus what sort of man would be suitable to be sent once more to Jerusalem, he said,
verses.3:38: "If you have any enemy or plotter against state affairs, send him there, and you will receive him back flogged, if indeed he even survives, because there is truly a certain power of God around the place.
verses.3:39: For He Himself who has His dwelling in heaven is the watcher and helper of that place, and He strikes and destroys those who come to do harm."
verses.3:40: And the events concerning Heliodorus and the preservation of the treasury turned out in this way.
verses.4:1: Now the aforementioned Simon, who had become an informer concerning the money and his homeland, was slandering Onias, claiming that it was he who had terrorized Heliodorus and had proved to be the author of the evils.
verses.4:2: And he dared to call the benefactor of the city, the guardian of his fellow nationals, and a zealot for the laws a plotter against the affairs of state.
verses.4:3: Now as the hostility progressed to such an extent that murders were even being committed through one of those approved by Simon,
verses.4:4: Onias, perceiving the severity of the contention and that Apollonius son of Menestheus, the governor of Coele-Phoenicia and Syria, was increasing the wickedness of Simon,
verses.4:5: prepared himself to go to the king, not becoming an accuser of the citizens, but looking to what was beneficial both publicly and privately for the entire multitude.
verses.4:6: For he saw that without royal oversight it was impossible to obtain peace for the affairs of state, and that Simon would not cease from his folly.
verses.4:7: Now when Seleucus departed this life and Antiochus, who was called Epiphanes, received the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias obtained the high priesthood by corrupt means,
verses.4:8: promising the king through a petition three hundred sixty talents of silver, and eighty talents from some other revenue.
verses.4:9: In addition to these, he also promised to pay another one hundred fifty, if it were granted by his authority for him to establish a gymnasium and a youth corps, and to enroll those in Jerusalem as Antiochenes.
verses.4:10: When the king consented and he gained control of the office, he immediately shifted his fellow countrymen over to the Greek way of life.
verses.4:11: And setting aside the royal concessions established for the Jews through John the father of Eupolemus, who conducted the embassy for friendship and alliance to the Romans, and abolishing the lawful civic institutions, he introduced unlawful customs.
verses.4:12: For he gladly established a gymnasium right beneath the citadel itself, and subjecting the noblest of those of our time, he brought them under the broad-brimmed hat.
verses.4:13: And such was the height of Hellenism and the advance of foreign ways, because of the extreme impurity of the impious Jason, who was no high priest,
verses.4:14: that the priests were no longer eager for the services of the altar, but despising the temple and neglecting the sacrifices, they hurried to take part in the unlawful exhibition in the wrestling arena after the summons of the discus,
verses.4:15: and counting ancestral honors as nothing, while considering Greek glories the finest.
verses.4:16: Because of these things as well, harsh adversity surrounded them, and those very people whose ways of life they emulated and whom they wished to resemble in every respect, they had as their enemies and punishers.
verses.4:17: For to act impiously against the divine laws is no light matter; rather, the time that follows will make these things clear.
verses.4:18: Now when a five-year contest was being held in Tyre and the king was present,
verses.4:19: the vile Jason sent envoys, as Antiochenes from Jerusalem, carrying three hundred drachmas of silver for the sacrifice to Heracles, which even those who carried them requested not be used for a sacrifice,
verses.4:20: but on account of those present, for the construction of the triremes.
verses.4:21: Now when Apollonius son of Menestheus was sent to Egypt for the enthronement of King Philometor, Antiochus, learning that he was hostile to his established affairs, took thought for his own security; therefore, coming to Joppa, he arrived in Jerusalem.
verses.4:22: Magnificently welcomed by Jason and the city, he was received in with torchlight and shouts; and after that he marched into Phoenicia to encamp.
verses.4:23: After a period of three years, Jason sent Menelaus, the brother of the previously mentioned Simon, to carry the money to the king and to complete memoranda concerning necessary affairs.
verses.4:24: But he, having been introduced to the king and having extolled him with the appearance of authority, diverted the high priesthood to himself, outbidding Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
verses.4:25: Having received the royal mandates, he arrived, bringing nothing worthy of the high priesthood, but having the passions of a cruel tyrant and the rages of a savage beast.
verses.4:26: And Jason, who had corruptly supplanted his own brother, being corruptly supplanted by another, had been driven as a fugitive into the land of Ammanitis.
verses.4:27: Meanwhile, Menelaus held control of the office, yet he made no regular payment of the money promised to the king,
verses.4:28: even though Sostratus, the commander of the citadel, kept demanding payment (for to him belonged the collection of the revenues); for which reason the two of them were summoned by the king.
verses.4:29: And Menelaus left behind his own brother Lysimachus as deputy of the high priesthood, while Sostratus left Crates, who was over the Cypriots.
verses.4:30: While such matters were taking place, it happened that the people of Tarsus and Mallus revolted, because they were being given as a gift to Antiochis, the king's concubine.
verses.4:31: Therefore the king went hastily to settle affairs, leaving behind as his deputy Andronicus, one of those in high rank.
verses.4:32: Now Menelaus, thinking that he had gained a favorable opportunity, stole some of the gold vessels of the temple and presented them as gifts to Andronicus, while others he had already sold to Tyre and the surrounding cities.
verses.4:33: And when Onias clearly learned of this, he reported it, having withdrawn to a place of sanctuary at Daphne, which lies near Antioch.
verses.4:34: Therefore Menelaus, taking Andronicus aside privately, urged him to kill Onias. So he came to Onias, and having been persuaded to deceit and pledging friendship with oaths, giving his right hand, even though he lay under suspicion, he persuaded him to come out from the sanctuary; and immediately he dispatched him, showing no respect for justice.
verses.4:35: For this reason, not only Jews, but also many of the other nations were indignant and distressed at the unjust murder of the man.
verses.4:36: When the king returned from the regions of Cilicia, the Jews in the city appealed to him, with the Greeks also sharing their hatred of the wickedness, because Onias had been killed without reason.
verses.4:37: Therefore Antiochus, grieved to his soul, moved to pity, and weeping because of the self-control and great orderly conduct of the one who had departed,
verses.4:38: and inflamed with fury, immediately stripped off Andronicus's purple robe, tore off his tunics, led him around through the whole city to the very place where he had acted impiously against Onias, and there put the murderer out of the way, as the Lord repaid him the punishment he deserved.
verses.4:39: Now when many acts of temple robbery had been committed in the city by Lysimachus with the consent of Menelaus, and the report had spread abroad, the multitude gathered together against Lysimachus, for many gold vessels had already been carried away.
verses.4:40: Now as the crowds were being stirred up and filled with rage, Lysimachus armed about three thousand men and initiated unjust violence, led by a certain Auranus, a man advanced in age and no less so in ignorance.
verses.4:41: When they also perceived the attack of Lysimachus, some snatched up stones, others thick pieces of wood, and some grabbed handfuls of the ashes lying nearby, and hurled them in confusion at those around Lysimachus.
verses.4:42: For this reason, they left many of them wounded, struck down some, and drove all of them to flight, while the temple-robber himself they killed beside the treasury.
verses.4:43: Concerning these matters, a trial was instituted against Menelaus.
verses.4:44: When the king arrived in Tyre, the three men sent by the council of elders presented the case before him.
verses.4:45: Already defeated, Menelaus promised considerable money to Ptolemy son of Dorymenes to persuade the king.
verses.4:46: Therefore Ptolemy took the king aside into a certain colonnade, as if for him to cool off, and changed his mind.
verses.4:47: And Menelaus, the cause of the entire wickedness, he acquitted of the charges, while for those wretched men, who even if they had spoken before Scythians would have been acquitted as blameless, for them he decreed death.
verses.4:48: Quickly, therefore, those who had spoken on behalf of the city, the peoples, and the sacred vessels suffered the unjust penalty.
verses.4:49: For this reason, even the Tyrians, hating the wickedness, magnificently provided what was needed for their funeral.
verses.4:50: But Menelaus, because of the greed of those in power, remained in office, growing in wickedness, having proved to be a great plotter against the citizens.
verses.5:1: Now about this time Antiochus made his second expedition into Egypt.
verses.5:2: And it happened that throughout the whole city, for almost forty days, there appeared horsemen racing through the air, wearing robes interwoven with gold, and fully armed with spears in companies,
verses.5:3: and the drawing of swords, and squadrons of horses drawn up in order, and attacks and charges taking place on both sides, and movements of shields, and multitudes of toils, and volleys of missiles, and flashes of golden ornaments, and armor of every kind.
verses.5:4: Therefore everyone prayed that the apparition had occurred for good.
verses.5:5: Now when a false rumor arose that Antiochus had departed life, Jason took with him not fewer than a thousand men and suddenly carried out an assault against the city; and when those on the wall were driven back, and in the end the city was already being captured, Menelaus fled into the citadel.
verses.5:6: And Jason carried out slaughters of his own people of the city mercilessly, not realizing that good fortune against kinsmen is the greatest misfortune, but thinking that he was winning trophies over enemies and not over people of his own nation.
verses.5:7: He did not gain control of the government, but receiving disgrace as the outcome of his plot, he passed again as a fugitive into Ammanitis.
verses.5:8: In the end, therefore, he met with an evil ruin: imprisoned by Aretas the tyrant of the Arabs, fleeing from city to city, pursued by all, hated as an apostate from the laws and abhorred as the executioner of his homeland and citizens, he was cast ashore into Egypt.
verses.5:9: He who had exiled many from their homeland perished in a foreign land, having set sail to the Lacedaemonians in the hope of obtaining shelter because of their kinship;
verses.5:10: and he who had cast out a multitude unburied went unmourned, and had no share in any funeral at all nor in ancestral law.
verses.5:11: Now when reports concerning what had happened reached the king, he concluded that Judea was in revolt; therefore, breaking camp from Egypt, raging like a wild beast in his soul, he took the city by force of arms.
verses.5:12: And he ordered the soldiers to cut down mercilessly those they encountered, and to slaughter those climbing up in the houses.
verses.5:13: And there was a killing of young and old, a wiping out of boys and women and children, and slaughters of virgins and infants.
verses.5:14: And eighty thousand were destroyed within three days in all, forty thousand in hand-to-hand fighting, and no fewer than those who were slaughtered were sold.
verses.5:15: And not satisfied with these things, he dared to enter the most holy temple of all the earth, having Menelaus as his guide, the one who had become a traitor both to the laws and to his homeland,
verses.5:16: and taking the sacred vessels with his polluted hands, and sweeping away with his profane hands the things set up by many kings for the advancement and glory and honor of the place.
verses.5:17: And Antiochus was lifted up in his mind, not perceiving that because of the sins of those who inhabited the city the Sovereign had been angry for a brief time, and therefore a disregard had occurred concerning the place.
verses.5:18: For if it had not happened that they were entangled in many sins, just as it was with Heliodorus who was sent by Seleucus the king for the inspection of the treasury, this man, upon advancing, would immediately have been scourged and turned back from his audacity.
verses.5:19: However, the Lord did not choose the nation because of the place, but the place because of the nation.
verses.5:20: Therefore the place itself also, having shared in the misfortunes that befell the nation, afterward shared in the benefits; and that which was overtaken in the wrath of the Almighty was restored again with all glory in the reconciliation of the great Sovereign.
verses.5:21: So Antiochus, having carried off eighteen hundred talents from the temple, hurriedly departed to Antioch, thinking in his arrogance that he could make the land navigable and the sea passable on foot, because of the loftiness of his heart.
verses.5:22: He also left behind overseers to afflict the race: in Jerusalem, Philip, a Phrygian by birth, yet having a character more barbarous than the one who appointed him;
verses.5:23: and at Gerizim, Andronicus; and in addition to these, Menelaus exalted himself over the citizens worse than the others, while holding a hostile disposition toward the Jewish citizens.
verses.5:24: And he sent Apollonius, the commander of the Mysians, with an army of twenty-two thousand, ordering him to slaughter all who were of full age, and to sell the women and the younger ones.
verses.5:25: When this man arrived in Jerusalem and pretended to be peaceful, he waited until the holy day of the Sabbath; and finding the Jews at rest, he ordered a muster in full armor for those under him.
verses.5:26: And he stabbed to death all who came out for the spectacle, and rushing into the city with weapons, he stationed great multitudes.
verses.5:27: But Judas, who is also called Maccabeus, as one of about ten, withdrew and lived in the mountains in the manner of wild beasts along with those who were with him; and they continued feeding on plant food, so as not to share in the defilement.
verses.6:1: Not long afterward the king sent out an elderly Athenian to compel the Jews to depart from the ancestral laws and not to live by the laws of God,
verses.6:2: and also to defile the temple in Jerusalem and call it by the name of Olympian Zeus, and the one at Gerizim, just as those who inhabited the place happened to be, by that of Zeus the Friend of Strangers.
verses.6:3: And the onslaught of evil was harsh and altogether hard to bear.
verses.6:4: For the temple was filled with debauchery and revelry by the Gentiles, who dallied with prostitutes and had intercourse with women in the sacred areas of the precincts, and moreover brought inside things that were not fitting.
verses.6:5: And the altar was filled with unlawful things prohibited by the laws.
verses.6:6: And it was possible neither to keep the Sabbath, nor to observe the ancestral festivals, nor simply to confess oneself to be a Jew.
verses.6:7: And with bitter compulsion they led them on the monthly birthday of the king to the eating of sacrifices; and when the festival of Dionysus occurred, they were forced to march in procession for Dionysus wearing ivy.
verses.6:8: And a decree went out to the neighboring Greek cities, at the suggestion of Ptolemy, to carry out the same policy against the Jews and to have them eat of the sacrifices,
verses.6:9: and to slaughter those who did not choose to pass over to Greek ways. One could therefore see the present misery.
verses.6:10: For two women were brought up for having circumcised their children; and having hung the infants from their breasts and led them publicly around the city, they hurled them down from the wall.
verses.6:11: And others, having run together into the nearby caves to keep the seventh day secretly, when betrayed to Philip, were burned to death together, because they had scruples against defending themselves out of regard for the glory of that most revered day.
verses.6:12: Therefore I urge those who read this book not to be disheartened because of the calamities, but to consider that the punishments are not for destruction, but for the discipline of our race.
verses.6:13: For indeed, that those who act impiously are not left alone for a long time, but immediately meet with penalties, is a sign of great kindness.
verses.6:14: For unlike with the other nations, where the Sovereign waits patiently to punish them until they have reached the full measure of their sins, He did not decide for it to be so with us,
verses.6:15: so that He would not later take vengeance on us when our sins have reached their end.
verses.6:16: Therefore He never withdraws His mercy from us; and though He disciplines with calamity, He does not forsake His own people.
verses.6:17: However, let these things be said by us by way of reminder; and after a few words we must proceed to the narrative.
verses.6:18: Eleazar, one of the foremost scribes, a man already advanced in age and most noble in the appearance of his face, was being forced to open his mouth wide and eat pork.
verses.6:19: But he, welcoming death with honor rather than life with pollution, went forward of his own accord to the rack,
verses.6:20: having spat it out, in the manner in which those ought to come forward who have the resolve to reject things that it is not lawful to taste for love of life.
verses.6:21: Now those who were appointed over the unlawful eating of sacrifices, because of their acquaintance with the man from former times, took him aside privately and called upon him to bring meat that it was proper for him to use, prepared by himself, and to pretend to be eating the portions of the sacrificial meat commanded by the king,
verses.6:22: so that by doing this he might be released from death, and because of his old friendship with them might obtain humane treatment.
verses.6:23: But he, adopting a noble resolve worthy of his age and of the dignity of his old age and of his acquired and distinguished way of life and of his most excellent conduct from childhood, and still more in accordance with the holy and God-established legislation, declared himself, telling them to send him quickly to Hades:
verses.6:24: "For it is not worthy of our age to pretend, so that many of the young, supposing that ninety-year-old Eleazar has gone over to foreign ways,
verses.6:25: should themselves, because of my pretense and for the sake of this brief and fleeting life, be led astray through me, and I should acquire pollution and a stain upon my old age.
verses.6:26: For even if for the present I should escape the punishment from men, yet neither alive nor dead will I escape the hands of the Almighty.
verses.6:27: Therefore, by courageously departing life now, I will show myself worthy of my old age,
verses.6:28: and will have left to the young a noble example of how to die a good death willingly and nobly for the revered and holy laws." And having said these things, he immediately went to the rack,
verses.6:29: while these men turned their goodwill toward him of a little earlier into ill will because of the madness, as they supposed, of the words just spoken.
verses.6:30: And when he was about to die from the blows, he groaned aloud and said, "To the Lord who has holy knowledge it is clear that though I could be released from death, I endure severe pains in my body as I am scourged, yet in my soul I gladly suffer these things because of fear of Him."
verses.6:31: So in this manner this man also departed life, leaving his own death not only for the young, but also for the majority of the nation, as an example of nobility and a memorial of virtue.
verses.7:1: Now it also happened that seven brothers, having been arrested together with their mother, were forced by the king to partake of the unlawful pork, being tormented with whips and thongs.
verses.7:2: And one of them, becoming spokesman, said, "Are you intending to question and learn from us? For we are ready to die rather than to transgress ancestral laws."
verses.7:3: And becoming furious, the king commanded pans and cauldrons to be heated red-hot.
verses.7:4: And when these were heated red-hot at once, he commanded them to cut out the tongue of the one who had become their spokesman and, after scalping him, to cut off his extremities, while the rest of the brothers and their mother looked on.
verses.7:5: And when he had become helpless in what remained, he ordered him to be brought to the fire while still breathing and to be fried. And as the vapor from the pan spread widely, they encouraged one another together with their mother to die nobly, saying this:
verses.7:6: "The Lord God looks on, and in truth has compassion on us, just as Moses made clear through the song that bears witness face to face, saying, 'And He will have compassion on His servants.'"
verses.7:7: Now when the first had passed away in this manner, they brought the second to the mockery; and tearing off the skin of his head along with the hair, they asked, "Will you eat before your body is punished limb by limb?"
verses.7:8: But answering in the ancestral language, he replied, "No." Therefore also
verses.7:9: this one received the torture in turn, like the first. And when he was at his last breath, he said, "You indeed, accursed wretch, release us from this present life, but the King of the world will raise us up, since we have died for His laws, to an eternal renewal of life."
verses.7:10: And after him the third was mocked, and when asked for his tongue he quickly put it out, and courageously stretched out his hands;
verses.7:11: and nobly he said, "From heaven these have been called, and because of His laws I disregard these, and from Him I hope to receive these again."
verses.7:12: So the king himself and those with him were astonished at the young man's soul, how he counted the pains as nothing.
verses.7:13: And when this one also had passed away, they tortured the fourth in the same way, tormenting him.
verses.7:14: And when he was near death, he spoke as follows: "It is preferable, when passing away at the hands of men, to look for the hopes from God of being raised up again by Him; for indeed there will be no resurrection to life for you."
verses.7:15: And next, bringing forward the fifth, they tormented him.
verses.7:16: But looking at him, he said, "Having authority among men, you do what you wish, mortal though you are; yet do not suppose that our race has been abandoned by God.
verses.7:17: But wait patiently, and watch His majestic power, how He will torture you and your offspring."
verses.7:18: And after him they brought the sixth, and when he was about to die, he said, "Do not be deceived any further, for we suffer these things because of ourselves, having sinned against our own God; things worthy of astonishment have happened;
verses.7:19: but as for you, do not think that you will go unpunished, having attempted to fight against God."
verses.7:20: Now the mother was exceedingly good and worthy of good remembrance, who, looking on as seven sons perished within the span of a single day, bore it with good courage because of her hopes in the Lord.
verses.7:21: And she encouraged each of the men in the ancestral language, filled with noble resolve and stirring up her womanly reasoning with manly courage, saying to them:
verses.7:22: "I do not know how you appeared in my womb, nor was it I who granted you spirit and life, and it was not I who arranged the elements of each of you.
verses.7:23: Therefore the Creator of the world, who formed the origin of man and devised the origin of all things, gives back to you both spirit and life again with mercy, just as you now disregard yourselves because of His laws."
verses.7:24: Now Antiochus, thinking he was being held in contempt and suspecting the reproachful voice, while the youngest was still alive, not only made his appeal through words, but also assured him with oaths that he would at once make him rich and enviable, if indeed he turned away from the ancestral customs, and that he would have him as a friend and entrust him with offices.
verses.7:25: But since the young man paid no attention at all, the king summoned the mother and urged her to become an adviser to the youth for his safety.
verses.7:26: And after he had urged her at length, she agreed to persuade her son.
verses.7:27: And leaning down toward him, deriding the cruel tyrant, she spoke as follows in the ancestral language: "Son, have mercy on me, who carried you in my womb for nine months, and nursed you for three years, and reared you and brought you to this age and nurtured you.
verses.7:28: I implore you, child, to look up to heaven and earth and, seeing all things in them, to recognize that God did not make them out of things that exist, and that the race of men comes into being in this way.
verses.7:29: Do not fear this executioner, but proving worthy of your brothers, accept death, so that in that mercy I may receive you back together with your brothers."
verses.7:30: While she was still concluding, the young man said, "What are you waiting for? I do not obey the command of the king, but I heed the command of the law that was given to our fathers through Moses.
verses.7:31: And you, who have become the contriver of every evil against the Hebrews, will by no means escape the hands of God.
verses.7:32: For we are suffering because of our own sins;
verses.7:33: and if for the sake of rebuke and discipline our living Lord has become angry for a little while, He will yet again be reconciled with His own servants.
verses.7:34: But you, unholy and most vile of all men, do not lift yourself up in vain, acting insolently with uncertain hopes, having raised your hand against the heavenly children;
verses.7:35: for you have not yet escaped the judgment of the Almighty, all-seeing God.
verses.7:36: For our brothers now, having endured a brief pain, have fallen under God's covenant of everlasting life; but you, by the judgment of God, will receive the just penalties for your arrogance.
verses.7:37: And I, just as my brothers did, give up both body and fortune for the ancestral laws, as we call upon God quickly to become gracious to the nation, and for you, with trials and whips, to confess that He alone is God,
verses.7:38: and in me and my brothers to halt the wrath of the Almighty, which has been justly brought upon our whole race."
verses.7:39: And becoming furious, the king dealt with this one most cruelly, beyond the others, bitterly resenting the derision.
verses.7:40: So this one also passed away undefiled, trusting completely in the Lord.
verses.7:41: And last, after her sons, the mother died.
verses.7:42: Now then, let the matters concerning the sacrificial meals and the excessive torments be set forth to this extent.
verses.8:1: Now Judas, who was also called Maccabeus, and those with him, slipping secretly into the villages, summoned their relatives, and enlisting those who had remained in Judaism, they gathered about six thousand.
verses.8:2: And they called upon the Lord to look upon the people who were oppressed by all, and also to have compassion on the temple that had been profaned by the ungodly men,
verses.8:3: and also to have mercy on the city that was being destroyed and was about to become level with the ground, and to listen to the blood crying out to Him,
verses.8:4: and to remember also the lawless destruction of the innocent infants and the blasphemies committed against His name, and to show hatred of wickedness.
verses.8:5: Now once Maccabeus had formed an organized band, he was already becoming irresistible to the Gentiles, for the wrath of the Lord had turned into mercy.
verses.8:6: Coming unexpectedly, he would set fire to cities and regions, and seizing the strategic places, routing not a few of the enemies,
verses.8:7: he took especially the nights as helpers for such attacks; and the report of his valor echoed everywhere.
verses.8:8: Now when Philip observed that the man was little by little making progress and advancing more and more frequently in successes, he wrote to Ptolemy, the governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, to come to the aid of the king's affairs.
verses.8:9: And he quickly appointed and sent Nicanor the son of Patroclus, one of the First Friends, placing under his command not fewer than twenty thousand Gentiles of all nationalities to wipe out the entire race of Judea; and they also assigned with him Gorgias, a general well experienced in matters of war.
verses.8:10: Now Nicanor determined to pay in full for the king the tribute to the Romans, amounting to two thousand talents, from the capture of the Jews.
verses.8:11: And immediately he sent to the coastal cities, inviting them to the purchase of Jewish slaves, promising to hand over ninety slaves for a talent, not expecting the justice from the Almighty that was about to overtake him.
verses.8:12: Now word reached Judas concerning Nicanor's advance; and when he informed those with him of the arrival of the army,
verses.8:13: those who were cowardly and distrusted the justice of God fled and removed themselves from the place,
verses.8:14: while the others sold everything that remained, and at the same time begged the Lord to rescue those who had been sold by the impious Nicanor before they even met him,
verses.8:15: and if not for their own sake, yet for the sake of the covenants with their fathers, and because of the calling of His revered and majestic name upon them.
verses.8:16: Now Maccabeus, having gathered those around him, six thousand in number, urged them not to be terrified by the prisoners nor to fear the great multitude of the Gentiles who had come unjustly against them, but to fight nobly,
verses.8:17: keeping before their eyes the outrage lawlessly perpetrated by them against the holy place, and the torture of the mocked city, and moreover the abolition of the ancestral constitution.
verses.8:18: "For they trust in weapons and also in daring deeds," he said, "but we trust in the Almighty God, who is able with a single nod to seize both those coming against us and the whole world."
verses.8:19: And he also recounted to them the acts of help that had occurred in the time of their ancestors: both the one in the time of Sennacherib, how one hundred eighty-five thousand perished,
verses.8:20: and the battle that took place in Babylonia against the Galatians, how eight thousand in all came to the engagement along with four thousand Macedonians, and when the Macedonians were hard pressed, the six thousand destroyed the one hundred twenty thousand because of the help that came to them from heaven, and took much plunder.
verses.8:21: By these words, having made them courageous and ready to die for the laws and their homeland, he divided the army into four parts,
verses.8:22: appointing his brothers as leaders of each division: Simon, Joseph, and Jonathan, placing under each one thousand five hundred,
verses.8:23: and moreover also Eleazar. Having read aloud the sacred book and given the watchword, "God's Help," leading the first cohort himself, he engaged Nicanor in battle.
verses.8:24: And with the Almighty becoming their ally, they slaughtered more than nine thousand of the enemies, left the greater part of Nicanor's army wounded and maimed in their limbs, and forced them all to flee.
verses.8:25: And they took the money of those who had come to purchase them. After pursuing them closely for a considerable distance, they turned back from the region, being hemmed in;
verses.8:26: for it was the custom before the Sabbath, for which reason they did not prolong chasing after them.
verses.8:27: Having collected the weapons from them and stripped off the spoils of the enemies, they devoted themselves to the Sabbath, exceedingly blessing and giving thanks to the Lord, who had preserved them to this day, having appointed a beginning of mercy for them.
verses.8:28: And after the Sabbath, having distributed a share of the spoils to those who had been tortured, to the widows, and to the orphans, they divided the rest among themselves and their children.
verses.8:29: When they had carried out these things and made a joint supplication, they begged the merciful Lord to be completely reconciled to His servants.
verses.8:30: And clashing with the forces of Timothy and Bacchides, they killed more than twenty thousand of them, and thoroughly gained control of high strongholds, and divided spoils of greater value, making themselves equal sharers with those who had been tortured, and the orphans, and the widows, and moreover also the elderly.
verses.8:31: And having carefully collected the weapons from them, they stored them all in the strategic places, and brought the rest of the spoils to Jerusalem.
verses.8:32: They also killed the phylarch of those with Timothy, a most unholy man who had caused the Jews much grief.
verses.8:33: And while celebrating the victory in their homeland, they burned those who had set fire to the sacred gates, and Callisthenes, who had fled into a dwelling; and he received the fitting wage of his impiety.
verses.8:34: Now the thrice-accursed Nicanor, who had brought three thousand merchants for the sale of the Jews,
verses.8:35: humbled with the help of the Lord by those whom he considered to be the least, put off his glorious robe and, making himself solitary like a runaway slave, came through the inland country to Antioch, having succeeded beyond everything in the destruction of the army.
verses.8:36: And the one who had undertaken to make good the tribute to the Romans from the capture of those in Jerusalem proclaimed that the Jews had a Defender, and that for this reason the Jews were invulnerable, because they followed His appointed laws.
verses.9:1: Now about that time Antiochus happened to have retreated in disorder from the regions around Persia.
verses.9:2: For he had entered the city called Persepolis and attempted to rob the temples and hold down the city. Therefore, when the crowds rushed forward, they turned to the aid of weapons; and it happened that Antiochus, routed by the local inhabitants, made a disgraceful withdrawal.
verses.9:3: Now while he was at Ecbatana, word reached him of what had happened concerning Nicanor and those with Timothy.
verses.9:4: Carried away with fury, he thought to vent upon the Jews even the wrong of those who had put him to flight. Therefore he ordered the charioteer to complete the journey by driving without ceasing, though indeed the judgment from heaven was accompanying him. For thus he spoke arrogantly: "I will make Jerusalem a common burial ground of Jews when I arrive there."
verses.9:5: But the all-seeing Lord, the God of Israel, struck him with an incurable and invisible blow. As soon as he had finished the speech, an incurable pain of the bowels seized him, and bitter torments of his internal parts,
verses.9:6: most justly, since he had tormented the bowels of others with many strange afflictions.
verses.9:7: Yet he in no way ceased from his insolence, and moreover he was filled with arrogance, breathing fire in his fury against the Jews and commanding the journey to be hastened. And it even happened that he fell from the chariot as it rushed along at headlong speed, and suffering a severe fall, all the limbs of his body were wrenched out of joint.
verses.9:8: And the one who presumed against the waves of the sea because of his superhuman arrogance, and supposed he would weigh the heights of the mountains in a balance, was brought down to the ground and carried along in a litter, displaying the power of God plainly to all,
verses.9:9: so that worms even seethed out of the body of the impious man, and while he was still alive in agonies and pains, his flesh fell away, and because of his stench the whole army was weighed down by the decay.
verses.9:10: And no one was able to carry along the one who a little earlier thought he could touch the heavenly stars, because of the unbearable burden of the stench.
verses.9:11: At this point, then, broken as he was, he began to abandon much of his arrogance and to come to his senses under the divine scourge, his pains intensifying moment by moment.
verses.9:12: And not even being able to endure his own stench, he said these words: "It is right to be subject to God, and for one who is mortal not to think arrogant thoughts."
verses.9:13: Then the abominable man made a vow to the Master who would no longer have mercy on him, saying as follows:
verses.9:14: that the holy city, which he had been hurrying to come and make level with the ground and build into a common burial ground, he would declare free;
verses.9:15: and as for the Jews, since he had resolved not even to consider them worthy of burial, to destroy them along with their infants for wild beasts as food for birds, he would make all of them equal to Athenians;
verses.9:16: and the holy temple which he had formerly plundered he would adorn with the finest votive offerings, and he would restore all the sacred vessels many times over, and he would supply from his own revenues the expenses required for the sacrifices;
verses.9:17: and in addition to these things, he would also become a Jew and would visit every inhabited place, proclaiming the might of God.
verses.9:18: But when his pains in no way ceased, for the righteous judgment of God had come upon him, despairing of his own condition, he wrote to the Jews the letter written below, having the form of a supplication and containing these words:
verses.9:19: "To the worthy Jews, the citizens, hearty greetings, good health, and prosperity, from Antiochus, king and general.
verses.9:20: Be well, you and your children; and your own affairs will be according to your wish. Having my hope in heaven,
verses.9:21: I affectionately remembered your honor and goodwill. Having returned from the regions of Persia and fallen into an illness involving hardship, I considered it necessary to take thought for the common security of you all,
verses.9:22: not despairing of my own condition, but having great hope of escaping the illness.
verses.9:23: Yet considering that my father also, at the times when he campaigned in the upper regions, appointed his successor,
verses.9:24: so that if anything unexpected should happen and anything grievous should also go forth, those throughout the country, knowing to whom the affairs of state have been left, might not be disturbed;
verses.9:25: and in addition to these things, observing that the neighboring rulers and those bordering on the kingdom are watching for opportunities and awaiting what will happen, I have appointed my son Antiochus as king, whom I often entrusted and commended to most of you when hurrying up to the upper satrapies. And I have written to him what is written below.
verses.9:26: Therefore I urge and ask you, remembering the benefits both collectively and individually, that each one preserve his existing goodwill toward me and my son;
verses.9:27: for I am persuaded that he, aligned with my policy, will conduct himself gently and humanely toward you."
verses.9:28: So the murderer and blasphemer, having suffered the worst things just as he had treated others, ended his life by a most pitiable fate in a foreign land, in the mountains.
verses.9:29: And Philip, his foster brother, conveyed the body back; and fearing the son of Antiochus, he crossed over to Ptolemy Philometor in Egypt.
verses.10:1: Now Maccabeus and those with him, with the Lord leading them, recovered the temple and the city.
verses.10:2: And they tore down the altars that had been constructed in the marketplace by the foreigners, and also the sacred precincts.
verses.10:3: And after purifying the sanctuary, they made another altar; and striking sparks from stones and taking fire from them, they offered sacrifices after a period of two years, along with incense and lamps, and made the presentation of the loaves.
verses.10:4: After doing these things, falling on their bellies, they implored the Lord never again to fall into such evils, but if they should ever sin, to be dealt with by Him with gentleness, and not to be handed over to blasphemous and barbarous nations.
verses.10:5: Now on the day on which the sanctuary had been profaned by foreigners, it happened on that same day that the purification of the sanctuary took place, on the twenty-fifth of that same month, Chislev.
verses.10:6: And with gladness they observed eight days in the manner of Booths, remembering how a short time before, during the Feast of Booths, they had been living in the mountains and in the caves in the manner of wild beasts.
verses.10:7: Therefore, holding wreathed staffs and beautiful branches, and also palm branches, they gave thanks to Him who had granted success in purifying His own place.
verses.10:8: And they decreed with a common ordinance and resolution for the whole nation of the Jews to observe the tenth days every year.
verses.10:9: Now such were the events concerning the end of Antiochus, who was called Epiphanes.
verses.10:10: But now we will make known the matters concerning the supreme Antiochus, who was the son of the ungodly man, summarizing the chief evils of the cities.
verses.10:11: For when he took over the kingdom, he appointed a certain Lysias in charge of affairs, and chief commander of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.
verses.10:12: For Ptolemy, who was called Macron, taking the lead in maintaining justice toward the Jews because of the injustice that had been done against them, tried to conduct affairs with them peacefully.
verses.10:13: For this reason, being accused by the Friends before Eupator and hearing himself called a traitor at every turn because he had abandoned Cyprus, which had been entrusted to him by Philometor, and gone over to Antiochus Epiphanes, and not having maintained his authority with nobility, he poisoned himself and departed life.
verses.10:14: Now Gorgias, having become commander of the regions, maintained mercenaries and at every turn kept up war against his own people.
verses.10:15: Along with these, the Idumeans also, being in control of strategic strongholds, harassed the Jews, and taking in those who had fled from Jerusalem, they attempted to keep up war.
verses.10:16: But Maccabeus and his men, having made supplication and imploring God to become their ally, rushed against the strongholds of the Idumeans.
verses.10:17: And attacking them vigorously, they gained control of the places, and drove back all those fighting on the wall, and slaughtered those who came in their way, and killed no fewer than twenty thousand.
verses.10:18: Now when no fewer than nine thousand had fled together into two exceedingly strong towers that had everything for a siege,
verses.10:19: Maccabeus, leaving behind Simon and Joseph, and also Zacchaeus and those with him, sufficient for the siege of these, departed himself for places requiring urgent attention.
verses.10:20: But those with Simon, becoming greedy for money, were persuaded with silver by some of those in the towers; and taking seventy thousand drachmas, they allowed some to slip away.
verses.10:21: And when they reported to Maccabeus about what had happened, having gathered the leaders of the people, he brought an accusation that they had sold their brothers for silver by releasing the enemies against them.
verses.10:22: Therefore he put to death these men who had become traitors, and immediately captured the two towers.
verses.10:23: And succeeding in everything with the weapons in his hands, he destroyed more than twenty thousand in the two strongholds.
verses.10:24: Now Timothy, who had previously been defeated by the Jews, having gathered immense foreign forces and having assembled no small number of horses from Asia, arrived intending to take Judea captive by the spear.
verses.10:25: But Maccabeus and his men, as he drew near, in supplication to God, having sprinkled earth on their heads and bound their waists with sackcloth,
verses.10:26: falling down on the step opposite the altar, implored Him to be gracious to them, to be an enemy to their enemies and to oppose those who oppose them, just as the law also declares.
verses.10:27: And having finished their prayer, taking up their weapons, they advanced a considerable distance from the city; and when they drew near to the enemies, they stayed by themselves.
verses.10:28: Just as the dawn was spreading, both sides attacked: the one side having as a guarantee of success and victory, along with valor, their refuge in the Lord, while the other side appointed fury as the leader of their struggles.
verses.10:29: And as a fierce battle took place, five resplendent men on horses with golden bridles appeared from heaven to the adversaries, and two of them, leading the Jews,
verses.10:30: both taking Maccabeus between them and shielding him with their own full armor, kept him unwounded; while at the opponents they hurled arrows and thunderbolts. Therefore, confounded with blindness, they were cut to pieces, filled with turmoil.
verses.10:31: And twenty thousand five hundred were slaughtered, and six hundred horsemen.
verses.10:32: But Timothy himself fled for refuge into a stronghold called Gazara, a very strong fortress, where Chaereas was commander.
verses.10:33: And Maccabeus and his men gladly besieged the fortress for forty days.
verses.10:34: But those inside, trusting in the strength of the place, were blaspheming exceedingly and uttering unlawful words.
verses.10:35: And as the twenty-fifth day was dawning, young men from among those with Maccabeus, inflamed in their fury because of the blasphemies, attacked the wall, and with manly courage and savage fury cut down everyone who came in their way.
verses.10:36: And others likewise, climbing up against those inside during the distraction, set fire to the towers, and kindling fires, burned the blasphemers alive; while others hacked through the gates, and having let in the rest of the force, captured the city,
verses.10:37: and they slaughtered Timothy, who was hidden in a certain cistern, and his brother Chaereas, and Apollophanes.
verses.10:38: And when they had accomplished these things, with hymns and thanksgiving they blessed the Lord, who confers great benefits on Israel and gives them the victory.
verses.11:1: Now after an exceedingly short time, Lysias, the king's guardian and kinsman and the one in charge of the affairs of state, being greatly displeased over the things that had happened,
verses.11:2: gathered together about eighty thousand men and all the cavalry and marched against the Jews, reckoning that he would make the city a dwelling place for Greeks,
verses.11:3: and the temple subject to tribute, just like the other shrines of the nations, and that he would put the high priesthood up for sale year by year;
verses.11:4: in no way taking into account the might of God, but made overconfident by the tens of thousands of foot soldiers and the thousands of horsemen and the eighty elephants.
verses.11:5: And having entered Judea and drawn near to Beth-zur, which was a fortified place and about five schoinoi distant from Jerusalem, he pressed it hard.
verses.11:6: Now when Maccabeus and those with him learned that he was besieging the strongholds, with lamentations and tears they implored the Lord, together with the crowds, to send a good angel for the deliverance of Israel.
verses.11:7: And Maccabeus himself, being the first to take up weapons, urged the others to risk danger together with him and go to the aid of their brothers; and together and eagerly they rushed out.
verses.11:8: And while they were right there near Jerusalem, a horseman in white clothing appeared going ahead of them, brandishing golden arms.
verses.11:9: And all together they blessed the merciful God and were strengthened in their souls, being ready to pierce through not only men, but also the wildest beasts and iron walls;
verses.11:10: they advanced in battle array, having the ally from heaven, since the Lord had shown mercy to them.
verses.11:11: And hurling themselves like lions into the enemy, they struck down eleven thousand of them and one thousand six hundred horsemen; and they forced all of them to flee.
verses.11:12: And most of them escaped wounded and naked; and Lysias himself also escaped by fleeing disgracefully.
verses.11:13: Now not being without understanding, weighing within himself the defeat that had happened to him and realizing that the Hebrews were invincible because the mighty God was fighting as their ally, he sent to them
verses.11:14: and persuaded them to come to terms on all just conditions, and that he would also persuade the king, compelling him to become a friend to them.
verses.11:15: And Maccabeus consented to all that Lysias proposed, having regard for what was beneficial; for whatever Maccabeus submitted to Lysias in writing concerning the Jews, the scribe granted.
verses.11:16: For letters had been written to the Jews from Lysias, reading in this manner: "Lysias to the multitude of the Jews, greetings.
verses.11:17: John and Absalom, who were sent from you, having submitted the document written below, made a request concerning the matters indicated in it.
verses.11:18: Therefore, whatever needed to be brought before the king as well, I explained clearly, and what was admissible he granted.
verses.11:19: If, therefore, you maintain goodwill toward the affairs of state, in the future as well I will try to be a source of good things.
verses.11:20: And concerning these matters in detail, I have instructed both these men and those from me to confer with you.
verses.11:21: Farewell. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the twenty-fourth of Dios Corinthius."
verses.11:22: Now the king's letter read as follows: "King Antiochus to his brother Lysias, greetings.
verses.11:23: Now that our father has passed over to the gods, desiring that those of the kingdom, being undisturbed, should attend to the care of the Jews,
verses.11:24: having heard that the Jews do not approve of our father's change to Greek practices, but preferring their own way of life, request that their lawful customs be granted to them;
verses.11:25: choosing, therefore, that this nation also be free from disturbance, we decide that both the temple be restored to them and that they live as citizens according to the customs in the time of their ancestors.
verses.11:26: You will do well, therefore, to send to them and give them pledges, so that knowing our policy they may both be of good cheer and gladly carry on in attending to their own affairs."
verses.11:27: And the king's letter to the nation was as follows: "King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews and to the other Jews, greetings.
verses.11:28: Be well; it would be as we wish; and we ourselves also are in good health.
verses.11:29: Menelaus reported to us, wishing that you return home and attend to your own affairs.
verses.11:30: Therefore, to those who return home up to the thirtieth of Xanthicus, there will be a pledge with immunity,
verses.11:31: that the Jews may use their own expenditures and laws, just as before; and none of them will be harassed in any way concerning things done in ignorance.
verses.11:32: And I have also sent Menelaus to encourage you.
verses.11:33: Farewell. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth of Xanthicus."
verses.11:34: And the Romans also sent them a letter reading as follows: "Quintus Memmius, Titus Manius, envoys of the Romans, to the people of the Jews, greetings.
verses.11:35: Concerning the things that Lysias, the kinsman of the king, granted to you, we also approve.
verses.11:36: But as for the matters that he decided should be referred to the king, send someone immediately after considering these matters, so that we may have them as is fitting for us; for we are proceeding to Antioch.
verses.11:37: Therefore, make haste and send some men, so that we also may know what your mind is.
verses.11:38: Be in good health. In the one hundred and forty-eighth year, on the fifteenth of Xanthicus."
verses.12:1: Now when these agreements had been made, Lysias departed to the king, and the Jews occupied themselves with farming.
verses.12:2: But among the local governors, Timothy and Apollonius the son of Gennaeus, and also Hieronymus and Demophon, and in addition to these Nicanor the Cypriarch, did not allow them to remain settled and live in quietness.
verses.12:3: And the people of Joppa committed so great an act of impiety, inviting the Jews living among them to board the boats provided by them, together with their wives and children, as though no hostility existed toward them;
verses.12:4: and after the public decree of the city, when these also had accepted, as people wanting to live in peace and having no suspicion, once they had been led out, they drowned them, being no fewer than two hundred.
verses.12:5: Now when Judas learned of the cruelty that had been done to his fellow countrymen, he gave orders to the men with him,
verses.12:6: and calling upon God, the righteous Judge, he came against the murderers of his brothers, set the harbor on fire by night, burned up the boats, and stabbed to death those who had fled there for refuge.
verses.12:7: Because the town was shut up, he withdrew, intending to come again and uproot the entire citizenry of the people of Joppa.
verses.12:8: But when he learned that those in Jamnia also wanted to deal in the same way with the Jews living there,
verses.12:9: he attacked the people of Jamnia by night as well and set fire to the harbor together with the fleet, so that the glow of the light was visible as far as Jerusalem, a distance of two hundred and forty stadia.
verses.12:10: And when they had marched away nine stadia from there, as they were making their march against Timothy, Arabs attacked him, no fewer than five thousand, and five hundred horsemen.
verses.12:11: Now when a fierce battle took place, and Judas and his men succeeded through the help from God, the nomads, having been defeated, asked Judas to give them his right hand, promising both to give livestock and to benefit them in other respects.
verses.12:12: And Judas, supposing that they would truly be useful in many ways, yielded to keep peace with them; and having received right-hand pledges, they departed to their tents.
verses.12:13: He also attacked a certain city built with causeways, fortified and enclosed with walls, and inhabited by mixed nations; its name was Caspin.
verses.12:14: And those inside, trusting in the strength of the walls and their store of food, treated Judas and his men quite insolently, reviling them, and moreover blaspheming and speaking things that are not permissible.
verses.12:15: But Judas and his men, calling upon the great Sovereign of the world, who without battering rams and siege engines cast Jericho down in the times of Joshua, charged ferociously against the wall.
verses.12:16: And capturing the city by the will of God, they carried out an untold slaughter, so that the adjacent lake, having a width of two stadia, seemed to stream with blood and to be filled.
verses.12:17: And marching away seven hundred and fifty stadia from there, they made their way to the stockade and to the Jews called Tubieni.
verses.12:18: And they did not overtake Timothy in those places, for he had withdrawn from those places at that time without accomplishing anything, though he had left behind a very strong garrison in a certain place.
verses.12:19: But Dositheus and Sosipater, among the commanders with Maccabeus, marched out and destroyed those who had been left by Timothy in the stronghold, more than ten thousand men.
verses.12:20: And Maccabeus, having organized the army with him into divisions, set them over the divisions; and they advanced rapidly against Timothy, who had with him one hundred and twenty thousand foot soldiers, and two thousand horsemen in addition to the seven thousand.
verses.12:21: Now when Timothy learned of the advance of Judas, he sent ahead the women and the rest of the baggage to the place called Carnion; for the place was hard to besiege and difficult to approach because of the narrowness of all the places.
verses.12:22: And when Judas's division appeared first, and terror fell upon the enemies, and fear came upon them from the appearing of the One who oversees all things, they rushed into flight, one running one way and another another, so that they were often injured by their own men and impaled on the points of their swords.
verses.12:23: And Judas pressed the pursuit all the more vigorously, stabbing the wicked wretches, and he destroyed about thirty thousand men.
verses.12:24: And Timothy himself, falling among Dositheus and Sosipater and their men, begged them with great cunning to let him go in safety, because he held the parents of many and the brothers of others, and it would happen that these would be shown no regard.
verses.12:25: And when he had confirmed with many assurances his pledge to restore them unharmed, they released him for the sake of the safety of their brothers.
verses.12:26: Then marching out against Carnion and the temple of Atargatis, he slaughtered twenty-five thousand persons.
verses.12:27: And after the rout and destruction of these, he also campaigned against Ephron, a fortified city in which there were multitudes of all tribes; and strong young men stationed before the walls fought back vigorously, where there were abundant stores of war engines and missiles.
verses.12:28: But calling upon the Sovereign who with might shatters the forces of the enemies, they brought the city under their power, and struck down about twenty-five thousand of those inside.
verses.12:29: And breaking camp from there, they pushed on toward Scythopolis, which is six hundred stadia from Jerusalem.
verses.12:30: But when the Jews settled there testified to the goodwill that the people of Scythopolis had toward them, and their gentle treatment in the times of misfortune,
verses.12:31: they gave thanks and further urged them to remain favorably disposed toward the nation in the future as well; then they came to Jerusalem, since the Feast of Weeks was close at hand.
verses.12:32: And after what is called Pentecost, they pushed on against Gorgias, the governor of Idumea.
verses.12:33: And he came out with three thousand foot soldiers and four hundred horsemen.
verses.12:34: And when they drew up for battle, it happened that a few of the Jews fell.
verses.12:35: But a certain Dositheus, one of Bacenor's men, a strong horseman, kept hold of Gorgias, and seizing his cloak, was dragging him vigorously; and while he wanted to take the accursed man alive, one of the Thracian horsemen rushed upon him and cut off his shoulder, so Gorgias escaped to Marisa.
verses.12:36: Now when Esdris and his men had been fighting for a long time and were exhausted, Judas called upon the Lord to appear as their ally and to appear as leader of the battle;
verses.12:37: and beginning in the ancestral language the cry with hymns, he charged unexpectedly against Gorgias and his men and put them to rout.
verses.12:38: Then Judas gathered the army and came to the city of Adullam; and as the seventh day was coming on, after they had purified themselves according to custom, he spent the Sabbath there.
verses.12:39: On the next day, Judas and his men came, as by that time the need had arisen, to recover the bodies of those who had fallen and to bring them back with their relatives to the ancestral tombs.
verses.12:40: And under the tunics of each of the dead they found sacred tokens of the idols from Jamnia, from which the law barred the Jews; and it became clear to all that for this reason these men had fallen.
verses.12:41: Therefore, all of them, blessing the ways of the Lord, the righteous Judge, who makes hidden things manifest,
verses.12:42: turned to supplication, asking that the sin that had been committed might be completely blotted out. And the noble Judas urged the multitude to keep themselves free from sin, since they had seen before their eyes what had happened because of the sin of those who had fallen.
verses.12:43: And having made a collection man by man amounting to two thousand drachmas of silver, he sent it to Jerusalem to offer a sacrifice for sin, acting very well and honorably as he took resurrection into account.
verses.12:44: For if he had not expected that those who had fallen would rise again, it would have been superfluous and foolish to pray for the dead.
verses.12:45: Or if he was looking to the finest gracious reward laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, the thought was holy and godly. Therefore he made the atonement for those who had died, that they might be released from the sin.
verses.13:1: Now in the one hundred and forty-ninth year, word reached Judas and his men that Antiochus Eupator had come with multitudes against Judea,
verses.13:2: and with him Lysias, the guardian and the one in charge of affairs, each having a Greek force of one hundred and ten thousand foot soldiers, and five thousand three hundred horsemen, and twenty-two elephants, and three hundred scythe-bearing chariots.
verses.13:3: And Menelaus also joined them, and with great duplicity urged Antiochus on, not for the welfare of his homeland, but thinking that he would be established in office.
